build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: A railway network is visible with multiple stations, track sections, at least two switchable junctions or sidings, and moving train pieces constrained to the tracks. Trains advance along rails over time, not teleporting between nodes. Score 0 if no track network or moving trains are present.

Clicking or otherwise operating a switch visibly changes the route: switch blades, route arrows, or highlighted track segments update, and a train subsequently follows the changed path rather than its previous one. Score 0 if no switch interaction is present or switches are purely cosmetic.

Signal controls have red/green or stop/go states that visibly halt and release at least one train before a section or station. A train approaching a red signal stops and waits; toggling the signal to green releases it. Score 0 if no signal interaction is present.

The game prevents or warns about conflicts between trains through blocked sections, collision warnings, occupancy lights, or an incident state. Two trains cannot silently overlap on the same section without consequence or feedback. Score 0 if multiple trains can overlap with no warning or consequence.

A timetable, lateness meter, deadline, or shift timer creates time pressure and visibly changes as trains wait or arrive. The player can see whether services are on time or delayed. Score 0 if routing has no timing or schedule element.

At least three distinct train or service identities are visible — such as local, express, freight, or color-coded destination trains — with different priorities or station requirements that force the player to make routing trade-offs. Score 0 if every train behaves the same way.

The shift escalates beyond a single routing move: rush-hour density, urgent services, delayed arrivals, blocked sections, or a later phase that increases dispatch pressure so the player must juggle more conflicts over time. Score 0 if the game shows a static, non-escalating state.

A result or summary screen appears at shift end reporting performance — on-time arrivals, delays, incidents avoided or caused — and offers retry or title navigation without restarting the executable. Score 0 if the game has no end-of-shift state or result.

The HUD clearly shows active routes, signal states, station goals, train identity/priority, and on-time/delay status so the player can make informed decisions without guessing. Score 0 if no dispatch information is readable.

The flow connects title or scenario -> dispatch shift -> active train routing -> result or retry/title navigation without restarting the executable. Score 0 if any major transition is missing or broken.

Actions produce readable feedback: clicking a switch shows the route change, toggling a signal shows the state flip, trains visibly stop or start in response, and arrivals or conflicts produce a cue. Score 0 if interactions have no observable effect on screen.

Art direction is coherent across title, track diagram, trains, stations, signals, switches, HUD, and result screens — sharing a consistent palette, typography, iconography, and line weight that reads as one authored product. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

The track diagram and station elements look like designed schematic art — clean lines, distinct station shapes, readable junction geometry — rather than raw rectangles or debug wireframes. Score 0 if the map is unthemed geometric primitives.

Train sprites or icons are visually distinct per service type, with readable silhouettes, color coding, or styled shapes that communicate identity at a glance. Score 0 if trains have no visual representation or are indistinguishable from track elements.

Animation and feedback make dispatch decisions legible: trains move smoothly along tracks, switches animate or visibly flip, signals change state with a transition, arrivals produce feedback, and warnings draw attention without obscuring the map. Score 0 if nothing animates and all changes are instantaneous.
